question: Why did Everton choose Goodison Park rather than Walton Hall Park to host their Under-21s' Premier League International Cup fixtures in the 2025-26 season?
reference_answer: Because the Premier League International Cup pits Everton's Under-21s against the reserve sides of European clubs (Real Madrid, PSV Eindhoven, AS Monaco and RB Leipzig), and Walton Hall Park, where the Under-21s usually play, is a less-equipped sporting facility.

question: Who were considered to replace William Saliba when he had an injury on early September 2025?
As of late October 2025, why was the Premier League expected to have only one game on Boxing Day?
reference_answer: Because Boxing Day 2025 fell on a Friday and the 27-28 December weekend had to be a full Premier League round: the league is committed to giving broadcasters 33 weekends of fixtures, the expanded Champions League leaves fewer free midweeks, and the deal to scrap FA Cup replays gave the FA Cup exclusive weekends, which left room for only one game on Boxing Day itself.

question: Why was Liverpool FC's staff Christmas party at Liverpool Cathedral brought to an early close in December 2024?
reference_answer: The cathedral's staff ended the party early after an "incident" that the cathedral said was not in line with its core values. This came amid newspaper reports that suspected drug paraphernalia had been discovered at the event. Liverpool FC said it does not condone or tolerate illegal substances at its sites or events.
notes: Hedged in the source: the Guardian attributes the drug-paraphernalia detail to newspaper reports and does not confirm it; the cathedral and the club only speak of an unspecified 'incident'. The reference answer keeps that hedge. The article also mentions a separate staff medical incident that Liverpool FC calls unrelated - deliberately left out of the answer. The party was held on a Thursday night (12 Dec 2024); the article was published Saturday 14 Dec 2024, so 'December 2024' in the question comes from that. No other article on this story turned up via `related`.

question: As of 30 April 2026, what had been reported about Craig Bellamy's contract with Wales as a barrier to Burnley appointing him as their new head coach after Scott Parker's departure?
reference_answer: Sky Sports reported that Bellamy had two years left to run on his Wales contract, and the BBC reported that Burnley would have to pay a release clause of at least £700,000 to get him out of his contract with the Football Association of Wales.
notes: The two halves of the answer come from different outlets: BBC 59379 gives the release clause (at least £700,000, payable to the FA of Wales) and Sky 60563 gives the remaining contract length (two years). Neither article has both figures. Both also say Bellamy is attached to the Wales job and the Euro 2028 goal (BBC: relishing it; Sky: 'totally committed'), but that is not part of the answer. The BBC says Burnley see him as a serious candidate with no formal bids; Sky says there had been no contact from Burnley - not asked here. Guardian 9478 and BBC live-blog pages (e.g. 59350) mention Bellamy as a target but give no contract details, so they are not listed. I did not check every BBC live-blog fragment from 30 April for a repeat of the release-clause figure.

question: As of 29 March 2026, why had Tottenham decided to part company with head coach Igor Tudor after just seven games in charge?
reference_answer: The Guardian reported Spurs acted in a desperate attempt to halt their slide towards relegation: Tudor, with no previous experience of English football, could not master the demands of the competition, taking one point from five league matches and leaving Spurs one point and one place above the bottom three. The final straw was the 3-0 home defeat by Nottingham Forest.
notes: Sky 60511 (same day) also covers the exit (lost five of seven games, 3-0 Forest defeat) but frames it mostly as 'inevitable' timing rather than explaining why; not annotated. Corrected after approval by Claude (LLM) at the user's request, 2026-10-21: Sky 60511 added at level 1 — contrary to the drafter's note above, it gives the core reasons (five defeats in seven games, the 3-0 Forest loss leaving Spurs a point above the drop, no Premier League experience); the non-reason 'mutually agreed' removed from the answer.

question: As of 2 January 2025, how did Thomas Tuchel's attempt to bring Chelsea's goalkeeping coach Hilário into England's backroom team play out, from the coach's first reaction in October to the outcome and the reason it took the form it did?
reference_answer: In mid-October 2024 Tuchel wanted to take Hilário to England, but Hilário had not decided and told Chelsea he was in two minds. By 20 November he had resigned from Chelsea, because Chelsea were reluctant to let him do a job-share with England, and was set to join Tuchel's staff from 1 January. By 2 January 2025 Hilário had been added to Tuchel's England backroom staff as goalkeeping coach, alongside performance coach Nicolas Mayer and analyst James Melbourne.
notes: Story across three dates: 17 Oct (Guardian 1072, Hilario undecided), 20 Nov (Guardian 1578, BBC 30710, 90min 14963: resigned after Chelsea refused a job-share; the three are redundant with each other, each level 1 because none holds the October or January step), 2 Jan (BBC 32788: added to staff). Also read and left out: BBC 30903 (11 Nov gossip: England to hold more talks over adding Hilario, Telegraph-sourced; only a step in the middle, not needed), BBC 31285 (1 Jan: 'set to join', superseded by 32788), Guardian 3385 (March, after as_of, so 0). The question joins three asks (first reaction, outcome, reason); the reason is one clause of the same story.

question: As of 4 June 2026, how had Liverpool's search for a replacement for the sacked Arne Slot progressed, from the first agreement on terms to the final announcement, and what timing did the club want to meet?
reference_answer: On 2 June the Guardian reported that Liverpool had agreed a deal in principle with former Bournemouth head coach Andoni Iraola, who had been in talks with sporting director Richard Hughes and was set to sign a two-year contract; the club wanted the switch completed before the World Cup starts on 11 June. On 4 June Sky Sports reported that Liverpool had formally appointed Iraola, who had signed the two-year deal, and that although other candidates were considered, he was the only one Liverpool spoke to.
notes: Sky 61578 (talks begun) also belongs to this story but its stored date (2 June) conflicts with its in-text date (Saturday 6 June 2026), so I left it out; auditor may want to add it. question: As of 31 August 2025, what was being reported about whether Nicolas Jackson would still complete his loan move from Chelsea to Bayern Munich?
reference_answer: Reports on 31 August 2025 disagreed about whether the move was still alive. TEAMtalk said Jackson was determined to complete the Bayern transfer and was refusing to return to London after Chelsea pulled the move over Liam Delap's hamstring injury, with his agent still trying to resurrect it. BBC's gossip column said, citing Florian Plettenberg, that Bayern had withdrawn their bid. TEAMtalk quoted Plettenberg saying the deal was 'still on hold - not off', with Chelsea looking for another striker so Jackson could leave. The Guardian reported that Bayern had called off their attempt to revive the deal because Chelsea would consider only a permanent sale (Bayern wanted a loan), and that Jackson was due to return to London.
notes: Versions are time-stamped within 31 Aug 2025 and partly reflect the story moving (Bayern did agree a revised loan on 1 Sept - Guardian 5934, BBC 88365, 88398 - published after as_of, so deliberately excluded/level 0). Disagreement is real though: BBC 88449 cites Plettenberg as saying Bayern withdrew; TEAMtalk 73895 cites the same journalist saying 'on hold - not off'. 73885 (Guardian-style aside inside a Guehi article, TEAMtalk) only says Chelsea want a new striker so Jackson can go to Bayern, hence level 1 not 2. Read and left out: BBC 88484 (31 Aug deadline-day page) only repeats that Chelsea withdrew permission on Saturday and mentions acrimony - no 31 Aug status version; BBC 88533 and Guardian 5900 (30 Aug) report the cancellation itself and predate the 31 Aug reports; BBC 88558 (30 Aug) is the original 'set to join' report; 88365/88398/5934/73852 (1 Sept) are after as_of. Question ask 'what was being reported' neutrally; no outlet named.

question: As of 6 January 2026, how did Strasbourg go about finding a successor to Liam Rosenior while Chelsea were pursuing him as their new head coach?
reference_answer: Chelsea's move for Rosenior depended on Strasbourg (like Chelsea owned by BlueCo) lining up a quality replacement first, and candidates were being considered from 1 January. By 4 January, Filipe Coelho and Jean-Marc Kuentz were expected to take interim charge, with former Wolves manager Gary O'Neil a contender for the permanent job and Minnesota United's Eric Ramsay also considered. By 6 January, when Rosenior was confirmed at Chelsea, Strasbourg had finalised a deal for Gary O'Neil to be their manager.
notes: Story across 1-6 Jan 2026: precondition (7651, 7655, 7678, BBC 89895), shortlist (7702 on 4 Jan, plus Ramsay in 7655), resolution (7731, 6 Jan). No single article holds the chain; 7731 gives only the outcome and says the move 'was held up' without saying a replacement was required. All level 1 per the multi-doc rule; 7651/7655/7678/89895 are partly redundant on the precondition. Read and not annotated: Guardian 7733 (analysis of fan reaction, no Strasbourg successor), 7735 (Football Daily, no successor), TEAMtalk 77003 (appointment, no successor), 7727 (rumour column: Strasbourg goalkeeper target, not manager), 7657 (profile of Rosenior). question: What set off André Onana's physical clash with a supporter after Cameroon lost 1-0 to Cape Verde in September 2025?
reference_answer: After the defeat (Onana had failed to come off his line for Cape Verde's goal), fans stormed the pitch and one supporter approached Onana from behind with a phone in hand, apparently to film him or take a photo. Onana reacted angrily and shoved the fan away, his hand connecting with the supporter's face; the fan then threw a water bottle towards him before being ushered away.
notes: Single 90min article (tabloid tier). `related` returns nothing (no club in headline), so I could not look for other outlets covering the same incident; unverified. The article gives the month only by its publication date (12 Sep 2025); the match date itself is not stated, so the question says 'September 2025'. Phrase 'appearing to film or take a photo' is the article's own hedge.

question: In a YouTube interview in December 2024, what did Pep Guardiola say about whether he would ever coach another club after leaving Manchester City?
reference_answer: He ruled it out: he said he would not manage another club or move to another country to start the same process again, because he would not have the energy for it. He said a national-team job could be of interest, since that is different (not daily training and a game every three days).
notes: BBC 31791 (same day, 10 Dec 2024) says the same; both level 2. Detail where the outlets differ but the question does not ask: Guardian says the new contract runs to summer 2026 and names the Desmontadito channel; BBC says the extension runs until 2027 and names a celebrity chef, Dani Garcia, as interviewer. The Guardian wording 'more of interest' - the national-team remark is hedged in BBC ('Maybe').
